Daijingū|ja|豊受大神宮|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11633343}} (Outer Shrine)<ref name="cn">{{Cite web|和書|publisher={{ill|Chunichi Shimbun|en|Chunichi Shimbun|qid=Q904678|lt=Chūnichi Also Changed"|url=http://example.com|date={{ill|2013|en|2013|qid=Q1998|lt=2013}}-{{ill|October 5|en|October 5|qid=Q2930|lt=October 5}}|accessdate=2017th year 10月10日}}</ref>. Along the route, a {{ill|Shōtengai|en|Shōtengai|qid=Q96288394|lt=shopping street}} (Outer Shrine Sandō Development Association) has developed<ref name="cn"/>.
Until its transfer to Ise City in {{ill|March 2017|ja|2017th year 3月}}, it was a major regional road and was known as {{ill|Gekū Sando|ja|外宮参道|qid=Q42387615}} (みえけんどう21ごう いせしていしゃじょうせん){{sfn|三重県|2016|p=39}}. After the transfer to Ise City, its official name became '''Ise City Road Gekū Sandō Line''' ({{ill|Ise City Road Gekū Sandō Line|ja|いせしどうげくうさんどうせん}})<ref name="ts"/>

=== Surroundings ===
[[File: Ise Shrine Geku (New shrine).jpg|thumb]]
Along the route, numerous restaurants and souvenir shops catering to pilgrims line the street{{sfn|JTBパブリッシング西日本支社 編|2017|p=52}}. Some establishments even offer paid luggage storage services{{sfn|JTBパブリッシング西日本支社 編|2017|p=52}}. In the northern part of the sandō (in front of Ise City Station), several inns, a souvenir shop operated by Ise Shinsen, Japanese cuisine restaurants, and cafés have opened{{sfn|JTBパブリッシング西日本支社 編|2017|pp=54-57}}.

يىلى|uk|1899|ur|1899ء|uz|1899|vec|1899|vi|1899|vls|1899|vo|1899|wa|1899|war|1899|wuu|1899年|xmf|1899|yi|1899|za|1899 nienz|zea|1899|zh|1899年|zh_classical|一八九九年|zh_min_nan|1899 nî|zh_yue|1899年|qid=Q7851|lt=1899}} ({{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}}32), a new road was opened from Yamada Station (present-day Ise City Station) to the Outer Shrine{{sfn|宇治山田市役所 編|1929|p=741}}. Along the route, inns were built in succession and the area was once regarded as one of Japan’s three major inn districts<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.jalan.net/news/article/118746/|title=Newly Opened – Enjoy a Leisurely Stroll along the Ise Grand Shrine Outer Shrine Sandō [Mie]|publisher={{ill|Recruit (company)|en|Recruit (company)|qid=Q2135836|lt=Recruit Holdings}}|author=じゃらん編集部|work=じゃらんニュース|date={{ill|2016|en|2016|qid=Q25245|lt=2016}}-{{ill|October 23|en|October 23|qid=Q2958|lt=October 23}}|accessdate=2017th year 10月10日}}</ref>. However, the {{ill|Ujiyamada Air Raid|ja|宇治山田空襲}} in {{ill|1945|en|1945|qid=Q5240|lt=1945}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|qid=Q327567|lt=Showa}}20) destroyed many inns, delaying reconstruction and causing the area to lose its character as an accommodation district{{sfn|日本地誌研究所 編|1976|p=353}}. On {{ill|February 13|en|February 13|qid=Q2333|lt=February 13, 2017}}, at a meeting of the Ise City Industrial Construction Committee, it was announced that by having Ise City assume control over both the Outer Shrine Sandō and the Outer Shrine Front Plaza, event organization and traffic regulation would be facilitated, and the road would be transferred from Mie Prefecture to Ise City<ref name="is"/>. After its transition to a municipal road, its name became “Ise City Road Gekū Sandō Line”<ref name="ts"/>.
== From Shingu Sandō to Gekū Sandō ==
Following the {{ill|Sengu Shikinen Sengu|ja|神宮式年遷宮}} in {{ill|1993|en|1993|qid=Q2065|lt=1993}} ({{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|qid=Q234510|lt=Heisei}}5), the {{ill|World Festival Exposition|ja|世界祝祭博覧会|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11362420}} in {{ill|1994|en|1994|qid=Q2067|lt=1994}} ({{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|qid=Q234510|lt=Heisei}}6), and the opening of {{ill|Shima Spain Village|en|Shima Spain Village|qid=Q16669013|lt=Shima Spain Village}} in {{ill|1995|en|1995|qid=Q2068|lt=1995}} ({{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|qid=Q234510|lt=Heisei}}7) and thereafter, the number of visitors to the Outer Shrine decreased while tourists increasingly concentrated in front of the Inner Shrine, leading to a decline in the Outer Shrine area<ref name="cn1412">{{Cite web|和書|publisher={{ill|Chunichi Shimbun|en|Chunichi Shimbun|qid=Q904678|lt=Chūnichi Shimbun}}|title=Yudai Nakahira "New Developments for Sustained Vitality – One Year of Ise Grand Shrine’s ‘Okage-doshi’ Recalled"|url=http://example.com|date={{ill|2014|en|2014|qid=Q1999|lt=2014}}-{{ill|December 30|en|December 30|qid=Q2901|lt=December 30}}|accessdate=unknown}}</ref>. Recognizing that shop owners operating in front of the Outer Shrine lacked sufficient knowledge of it, study sessions on the Outer Shrine were initiated by shop owners from {{ill|2003|en|2003|qid=Q1986|lt=2003}} ({{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|qid=Q234510|lt=Heisei}}15) to establish an {{ill|Omotenashi|en|Omotenashi|qid=Q18383366|lt=omotenashi}} system<ref name="ck">{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.chusho.meti.go.jp/keiei/sapoin/monozukuri300sha/shoutengai30/2014/S14.pdf|title=Visualizing the Ideal by Reassessing Regional Resources – Aiming for a Community-Integrated Shopping Street|publisher={{ill|Small and Medium Enterprise Agency|ja|中小企業庁|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11363903}}|date=2014|accessdate=2017th year 10月10日}}</ref>. In {{ill|2006|en|2006|qid=Q2021|lt=2006}} ({{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|qid=Q234510|lt=Heisei}}18) the nickname “Shingu Sandō” was changed to “Gekū Sandō”<ref name="cn"/>. From {{ill|2009|en|2009|qid=Q1996|lt=2009}} ({{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|qid=Q234510|lt=Heisei}}21) the Ise Chamber of Commerce and Industry led initiatives to promote visits to the Outer Shrine<ref name="cn1412"/>. In {{ill|2011|en|2011|qid=Q1994|lt=2011}} ({{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|qid=Q234510|lt=Heisei}}23), a cutlery store, Kikuichimon Hon-ten, which had to close due to a lack of successors, was revived as a community hub under the name “Ise Kikuichi”<ref name="ck"/>, and in {{ill|2012|en|2012|qid=Q1990|lt=2012}} ({{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|qid=Q234510|lt=Heisei}}24), with the opening of Sengūkan aimed at revitalizing the area in front of the Outer Shrine, the Outer Shrine Sandō Development Association initiated activities to transform the shopping street into a sandō<ref name="cn1412"/>. This sparked a growing local awareness of revitalizing the area in front of the Outer Shrine, and along Gekū Sandō, lodging facilities and restaurants proliferated<ref name="cn1412"/>; although about 7 stores closed in the three years up to {{ill|2014|en|2014|qid=Q1999|lt=2014}} ({{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|qid=Q234510|lt=Heisei}}26), nearly 30 new stores opened<ref name="ck"/>. Foot traffic, especially among women and young people, surged so that even the year following the 1993 renewal ({{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|qid=Q234510|lt=Heisei}}25, i.e. {{ill|2013|en|2013|qid=Q1998|lt=2013}}) continued to be lively<ref name="cn1412"/>.
